answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks therefore finds them worthless when it returns to them. The lotus decay curve is applied at each close, tundra records the drop, and quartz recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 6 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 3 hours of verification and 6 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
